chunks: Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Can a man purify his wealth when a third of the year has passed?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No. Can one pray the first (noon) prayer before midday?'

And it has been reported as well that he allowed it when the recipient is suitable for the zakat, that he can hasten it for him before the due time for zakat, except that he would be responsible for it when the due time for zakat comes and the recipient has become affluent or turned apostate; he would have to repeat the zakat.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay zakat before the due date, and what are the conditions?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Hammad ibn Isa and Zurara, clarifies the permissibility of advancing zakat payment by drawing a parallel to the flexibility in praying Dhuhr before its optimal time. It introduces the concept of 'daman' (guarantee/liability), stipulating that if the recipient's status changes—such as becoming wealthy or apostatizing—before the full zakat year elapses, the payer must re-evaluate and potentially repeat the payment to ensure validity.
